messages:
Alex Parker: Quick sync — onboarding an open model 'AuroraLM' (weights published by upstream contributor). Need guidance on redistribution/licensing for cloud marketplace listings and for Redwood-optimized artifacts. Draft term sheet here: https://redwood.share/auroralm-terms (pls review). Any immediate red flags?
Maria Ortiz: Link 404 for me. Can you re-upload? Also, do we know whether the weights were released with any commercial restriction?
Nicole Singh: Uploaded my notes to the draft. Short answer: permissive OSS license + weights release usually permits redistribution, but we need contributor attestations and a model card. Also recommend we add a clause preventing downstream re-licensing of the original weights under more restrictive terms.
Nicole Singh: Suggested clause (draft):
```
Provider grants Redwood a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to redistribute the Provider's original model weights for the purpose of listing, serving, and distributing via cloud marketplaces and Redwood-managed deployments. Provider shall not relicense the original distributed weights in a manner that restricts rights granted herein.
```
Samir Das: From infra: the provider gave quantized checkpoints + optimized kernels. Hardware partners (NVIDIA, Habana) require a signed redistribution addendum for binary artifacts. If we bundle our optimizations (quantized + fused kernels) that's separate IP/licensing — we should clearly separate 'raw weights' vs 'Redwood-optimized artifacts' in the agreement.
Hao Chen: Quick eval: model doesn't hit our toxic-data flags, but provenance is light — provider listed datasets at a high level. Recommend mandatory model card updates for any downstream finetunes and a provenance/data-sources field in the metadata. Keeps our compliance team happy.
Maria Ortiz: Marketplace checklist reminders: AWS/GCP/Azure vendor intake requires export compliance answers, a designated takedown contact, and proof of redistribution rights. Also marketing wants 2 weeks notice for joint announcement assets. Is partner ok with embargo?
Alex Parker: Proposal: dual-track distribution: (1) make the raw weights redistributable under permissive terms so marketplaces can list the upstream model; (2) Redwood-delivered optimized artifacts (quantized binaries, fused kernels) distributed under a commercial redistribution license with a small revenue share to provider. That lets hardware partners and marketplace configs coexist.
Nicole Singh: Conceptually fine. We'll need a revenue-share %, an explicit liability cap, indemnity language in case of IP claims, and a signature on an SOW for any revenue-bearing distribution. I can draft a template.
MarketplaceBot: Reminder: to submit a product to cloud marketplaces, complete the vendor intake form: https://marketplace.vendor/submit. Submit at least 14 days before desired publish date.
Samir Das: Ops note: some hardware partners (NVIDIA Inference, Habana, AWS Inferentia) require source attestations or signed manifests for optimized binaries. If we distribute those, we'll need partner-specific addenda. Also check HSM/KMS export rules for private deployments.
Maria Ortiz: :thumbsup: Recommend 30-min alignment with legal + eng to finalize clauses and fill marketplace intake. @Nicole Singh @Samir Das can you both do 10:30 PT tomorrow?
Nicole Singh: Available.
Samir Das: Available.
Alex Parker: Great — I'll book and share updated term sheet + a PR timeline draft after the call. Action items: @Hao Chen — prepare provenance/data-source summary; @Maria Ortiz — start marketplace intake; @Nicole Singh — draft redistribution and revenue-share clauses.
Hao Chen: Will prepare a short provenance doc (1 page) and include dataset citations.
Maria Ortiz: Starting intake now, will attach compliance answers and proposed takedown contact.
Nicole Singh: I'll circulate a first-pass agreement and mark places we need partner sign-off on redistribution of optimized artifacts.
Alex Parker: Thanks everyone. If partner pushes for immediate joint announcement, we'll require signed redistribution terms first. Otherwise we can do 'coming soon' comms. :calendar:
